sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read source text with line selectors, raw views and precise continuation.
- bash: Run shell commands with owned background jobs and bounded output.
- edit: Apply tagged original-coordinate edits or unique exact-text replacements.
- write: Create or fully replace one file, optionally guarded by the revision you read.
- cd: Inspect or change the working location for coding tools.
- ask_user: Ask the user for explicit choices or missing information.
- jobs: Inspect, await, stop or send input to owned jobs.
- ls: List a directory with typed entries and a continuation cursor.
- grep: Search file contents with exact matches and honest limits.
- find: Find files by name glob under a directory.

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>

toolsAdded.description: Read text from local paths or registered scheme:// resources; relative paths use the Workbench location. Use path suffixes :N, :A-B, :A+C, :-N, comma ranges or :raw (for example src/main.go:20-40) when supported by the provider. Literal filenames win. Exactly one of path or paths (1–32) is required; explicit selector is for one path only. Output is bounded to 50 KiB/2000 lines across the batch; Details report actual source coverage and continuation. For local text, raw preserves source bytes; ordinary ranges include one preceding and three trailing lines.
toolsAdded.name: read

path.description: Local path or registered scheme URI, optionally with a supported selector suffix.

paths.description: Explicit ordered multi-read, sharing one output budget.

selector.description: Single-path selector when punctuation is ambiguous; cannot accompany a suffix.

toolsAdded.description: Run a local shell command in the captured Workbench location. Defaults: foreground, 120-second hard deadline, stdin closed. background returns a job ID immediately; yield_seconds promotes a still-running command after that delay. timeout_seconds=0 disables the deadline. interactive keeps stdin open for jobs write/eof. Cancellation terminates the owned process group. Output is bounded and reports its byte cursor and any eviction gap.
toolsAdded.name: bash

toolsAdded.description: Edit local UTF-8 files using either {hashline} tagged batches from read output, or {path, edits:[{oldText,newText}]} exact replacements. Tagged batches start with [path#TAG] copied from read. Use PUT 2.=2: (replace line 2), PUT 2.=5: (range), PUT >5: (insert after), PUT <1: (BOF), PUT >$: (EOF), or PUT 6*: (structural block); each literal payload row starts with +. edit.mode restricts the accepted branch: hashline, replace, or auto (both); there is never automatic fallback after a rejected patch. CUT, REM, MV and registers are supported. All coordinates refer to the original snapshot; block anchors require syntax evidence. Seen-line guards cover complete consumed ranges. Exact replacements must be unique and non-overlapping. Every resource is preflighted before writes, then locked and revision-checked immediately before atomic replacement. A partial I/O failure reports landed and unattempted effects; there is no rollback. Changed sources are relocated only when anchors are unambiguous; otherwise reread the current source.
toolsAdded.name: edit

toolsAdded.description: Create or fully replace a local file or declared writable provider resource; use edit for local partial changes. Relative paths resolve against the Workbench location. For local files, expectedRevision requires an unchanged file, content is written atomically, existing modes are preserved, and directories are not created. local://<name> writes a file into the session scratch (existing directory, 4 MiB maximum, no revision checks). Control writes also support job:// stdin and ctl, skill:// unload, agent://<id>/inbox, session://<id>/title and session://self/instructions/ctl; their own policy and confirmation rules apply.
toolsAdded.name: write

expectedRevision.description: Require the revision reported by read for a local file or writable provider resource; refused when it changed.

path.description: Local file, writable provider URI or supported control URI.

raw.description: Write literal content without interpreting copied tagged-read formatting.

toolsAdded.description: Inspect or change the Workbench working location without changing PiG's session cwd. Use {} for status, {path} for a local directory, or {reset:true} to return to the origin. Relative paths use the captured location. A change waits at most 2 seconds for active mutations and persists before activation.
toolsAdded.name: cd

reset.description: Return to the original session location.

toolsAdded.description: Ask 1–20 questions using native interactive dialogs. Supports single, multi, preview, freeform and secret questions, custom answers and notes. Blocks for the user's answers. Dismissal returns cancelled without partial answers; an elapsed dialog deadline returns timedOut. Print/JSON without UI returns interactionUnavailable. Secret values are stored encrypted and only placeholders appear in answers or session records.
toolsAdded.name: ask_user

toolsAdded.description: Inspect or control a session-owned shell job. action=list needs no id; status/output/wait/kill/write/eof require id. output uses a monotonic byte cursor; evicted bytes are reported. wait is cancellable without killing a background job; kill terminates its process group. write sends exact text and eof closes stdin.
toolsAdded.name: jobs

toolsAdded.description: List one container through the Workbench resource router, including registered scheme URIs whose providers support listing. Entries have typed kinds and a continuation cursor; incomplete listings are reported.
toolsAdded.name: ls

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous listing.

includeHidden.description: Include dot-prefixed entries; true by default.

toolsAdded.description: Search file contents at a local path or registered provider file/directory. Line selectors are accepted only for explicit files. Pass exactly one regex pattern, or literal patterns for an OR search (literal:true). Relative paths resolve against the Workbench location. Local traversal honors nested .gitignore rules; explicitly named file roots remain searchable. Binary, oversized and incomplete provider files are skipped and listed in Details; hitting a bound reports complete:false instead of pretending the results are exhaustive.
toolsAdded.name: grep

context.description: Number of surrounding source lines before and after each match.

exclude.description: File or directory name globs to skip.

filesOnly.description: Return distinct matching file paths without source text or context.

glob.description: File glob with *, ?, [class], {alternatives} and ** path components; use / separators.

literal.description: Treat patterns as literal text instead of a regex.

path.description: Local file/directory or provider URI; default is the Workbench location.

pattern.description: Regular expression, or one literal when literal is true.

patterns.description: Literal OR patterns; requires literal:true and cannot accompany pattern.

toolsAdded.description: Walk a local directory or registered provider root for file names matching a glob pattern. Links and noWalk subtrees are not followed, control files and .git are skipped, local .gitignore rules and exclusions apply, and bounds report complete:false.
toolsAdded.name: find

path.description: Directory to walk; default is the Workbench location.

pattern.description: File glob, e.g. *.go or **/*.{go,md}; slash patterns are relative to the named root.

content.text: Use the ls tool on the current directory, the find tool for *.txt files, the grep tool to search the whole project for the word TODO, and the read tool on src/main.go. Then answer with only the number of TODO lines you found.
